# Phase One — Boundless Geelooy Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos reveals a thousand doors yet leaves the hallway still and clear;
Awtsmoos.com should feel like tomorrow arrived, while every hidden power stays calmly near.

## North star

Turn `geelooy` into a coherent product system: every public page feels related, every advanced surface expands only when requested, every AI-facing contract is discoverable from data, every animation has purpose, and every mobile viewport remains contained.

## Interface universe

1. Mobile-first layouts with one-column defaults and progressive multi-column expansion.
2. Retractable navigation, inspectors, metadata, logs, toolbars, and secondary actions.
3. Surface-local CSS only: every selector anchored to a page/component root attribute or class.
4. No unscoped `body`, `html`, `button`, `a`, `input`, `*`, or generic utility selectors in new style modules.
5. Page-owned `@import` chains so dependencies are explicit and collision risk is inspectable.
6. Fluid type and spacing via bounded `clamp()` values, never fragile fixed desktop assumptions.
7. Container queries for reusable components where viewport media queries would couple unrelated pages.
8. Safe stacking tokens inside isolated stacking contexts rather than arbitrary four-digit z-index wars.
9. Overlay geometry using inset-safe sheets, maximum block sizes, scroll containment, and viewport-safe padding.
10. Interaction states for every relevant control: hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, busy, selected, expanded.
11. Reduced-motion behavior that preserves state meaning without decorative movement.
12. Futuristic motion from opacity, transform, filter, and subtle depth rather than layout-thrashing animation.
13. Touch targets sized for thumbs, with no hover-only affordances.
14. Keyboard navigation, semantic labels, focus restoration, Escape behavior, and dialog boundaries.
15. Skeleton/empty/error/success/offline states treated as designed states, not afterthoughts.
16. Overflow sentinels in testing to catch horizontal spill at 320, 390, 768, and desktop widths.
17. Theme values exposed through local custom properties on the component root, never global root mutation.
18. Cards that reveal dense metadata through `<details>`, drawers, tabs, or explicit advanced toggles.
19. Consistent compact command bars with search first, advanced filters second.
20. A visual language of luminous edges, restrained glass, crisp typography, and minimal chromatic noise.

## JavaScript architecture universe

21. Data first: route/product/tool definitions live in small immutable registry modules.
22. Class boundaries only where lifecycle/state/extension semantics are real, never ceremony for its own sake.
23. Named base contracts that can be extended by specialized adapters without branching everywhere.
24. Kabbalistic naming as a semantic layer: `Keli` for bounded containers/adapters, `Ohr` for emitted data/events, `Sefirah` for capability records, `Merkava` for composed systems, while public API names remain predictable.
25. Extensive JSDoc on every exported function/class plus meaningful private behavior.
26. Event and data payloads documented as schemas instead of implicit object folklore.
27. Abortable async work, deterministic cleanup, and explicit error boundaries.
28. Feature detection before optional browser APIs.
29. No hidden mutation across modules; state ownership must be obvious.
30. Stable public contracts wrapped around internal poetic architecture so third-party agents do not need project lore.

## Universal agent API universe

31. One machine-readable capability manifest describing auth, installation, tools, routes, versions, examples, and schemas.
32. One human quickstart that mirrors the manifest exactly.
33. Copy-safe install flows for terminal agents and browser/headless agents.
34. OAuth/PKCE and device authorization documented as first-class paths with immutable route identifiers.
35. Agent bootstrap endpoint returning the minimum next actions instead of forcing documentation scraping.
36. Versioned JSON schemas for requests, responses, scene descriptions, errors, and capability discovery.
37. Idempotency/request identity guidance encoded in examples so agents avoid duplicate mutations.
38. Dry-run/preview semantics for destructive or expensive actions when supported.
39. Structured errors with machine-readable codes, retryability, and next-step hints.
40. API examples in curl, JavaScript, and generic agent pseudocode generated from one source of truth.

## Advanced 2D cartoon universe

41. A data-driven scene graph where an AI can describe characters, props, backgrounds, poses, dialogue, camera, timing, and transitions in JSON.
42. `MerkavaScene` composition from small layers: background, actor, prop, text, effect, camera, audio cue.
43. Reusable character rigs with expressions, pose presets, anchor points, and palette tokens.
44. Timeline primitives for entrance, exit, tween, blink, lip cue, camera pan, cut, and speech bubble.
45. Constraint-based placement so agents specify intent such as `leftOf`, `lookAt`, `safeArea`, not fragile pixels.
46. Responsive scene fitting and letterboxing with no clipping on mobile canvases.
47. Deterministic seeded rendering for reproducible agent output.
48. Preview-first generation where an agent can validate a scene schema before rendering.
49. Export adapters for canvas, SVG where suitable, image sequences, and compact scene JSON.
50. Example recipes: two-character dialogue, explainer panel, comic strip, animated product walkthrough.

## Documentation universe

51. `/docs` becomes a progressive disclosure hub: Start, Build, API, Agents, 2D Scenes, Reference, Troubleshooting.
52. Every API concept includes the shortest working example first, then advanced details collapsed below.
53. Architecture diagrams rendered from small data descriptions, not hand-maintained contradictory prose.
54. Search and deep links for every capability and error code.
55. “Copy for agent” blocks that contain only executable context and contract facts.
56. Changelog/version compatibility notes close to affected APIs.
57. Accessibility and mobile behavior documented as part of component contracts.

## Verification universe

58. Static scans for global selectors, oversized fixed widths, dangerous viewport units, unexplained z-index values, and missing interaction states.
59. DOM overflow probes at small mobile widths.
60. Keyboard-only navigation probes for dialogs, menus, tabs, and drawers.
61. Reduced-motion and focus-visible checks.
62. API schema round trips and example validation.
63. Scene JSON validation and deterministic render smoke tests.
64. Route catalog checks for missing/dead products.
65. Readback of every touched file, syntax checks, targeted runtime checks, then planned-versus-actual delta review.

## Architectural restraint

The ideal is not one global framework poured over every page. The ideal is a family of small local foundations, imported explicitly by each surface, sharing data contracts and design principles without sharing unsafe selector scope. Power should be everywhere; clutter should be nowhere.
